input_drift.method: Population Stability Index, monthly, on all model features
input_drift.note: The macro-economic features (emp.var.rate, euribor3m, nr.employed) show PSI far outside the textbook 0-2 range used for the alert thresholds below -- this is expected given the 2008-2010 regime shift documented in Section 6.1 above (train/test barely overlap in range), not a bug in the PSI formula. A newly off-scale PSI on a *different* feature would be the actual anomaly worth investigating.

prediction_drift.method: PSI on predict_proba output, per scoring batch

realized_performance_tracking.method: Monthly: join actual outcomes back to that period's predictions, recompute PR-AUC and decile-level capture rate.
realized_performance_tracking.trigger: If capture rate in the top-called decile drops toward the population base rate, the ranking has stopped working, regardless of what input PSI says.

retraining_cadence.recommendation: Quarterly by default, immediately if any priority feature's PSI exceeds 0.25, OR if lift_based_retrain_trigger fires (see below) -- whichever comes first.
retraining_cadence.rationale: Notebook 01/04's regime-shift finding showed target rate and macro features can move dramatically within a single year; quarterly is a starting point, not a guarantee -- tighten if realized performance degrades faster than that in practice.

feedback_loop_guard.risk: If only the top-K% ever gets called, outcomes for the rest of the population are never observed again, and future training data becomes biased toward customers who already looked promising.
feedback_loop_guard.mitigation: Reserve a small (5-10%) random-exploration slice of every campaign, called regardless of score, so the next retraining cycle has unbiased outcome data across the whole score range.

lift_based_retrain_trigger.why_this_exists: notebooks/10_Robustness_Reliability_Backtest.ipynb's rolling-origin backtest found one out-of-time window (origin 4 of 7) where lift-over-naive was 0.77x -- worse than calling customers at random -- with a bootstrapped 95% CI of [0.72x, 0.85x] entirely below 1.0x (reports/rolling_origin_backtest.json). That is a statistically confirmed instance of the model actively hurting call-prioritization, not a borderline point estimate. A purely calendar-based quarterly cadence would not have caught this until the end of that quarter.
lift_based_retrain_trigger.metric: lift_over_naive = PR-AUC(top-called-slice) / population_positive_rate, computed monthly the same way realized_performance_tracking already does, using the current month's actual outcomes.
lift_based_retrain_trigger.trigger: If a rolling monthly lift_over_naive falls below 1.0x (or, once enough live volume accumulates to bootstrap a monthly CI, its 95% CI upper bound falls below 1.0x), retrain immediately -- do not wait for the next quarterly cycle or for a PSI threshold to also fire. Below 1.0x means the model is worse than not scoring at all for that period.
lift_based_retrain_trigger.relationship_to_quarterly_cadence: This trigger supersedes retraining_cadence's quarterly default when it fires; the quarterly cadence remains the floor (retrain at least that often even if lift stays healthy), this trigger is the ceiling on how long a confirmed sub-1.0x period is allowed to run before action.
